quote: Does acting this way make you stronger, or weaker?
content: The test is not empty; it is the instruction to state the cost of the precaution and the cost of the error, which is why every worked example reduces to an expected-value calculation. That is the point. The essay's complaint about "humility" is precisely that it floats free of any such calculation, and its remedy is to replace a virtue term with a decision, so an objection that the examples "need no virtue term at all" has restated the thesis. The degrees of freedom warning applies to principles that cannot be cashed out; this one can be, and the essay cashes it.

quote: Scientific humility is something you would practice even if you were alone in a spacesuit, light years from Earth with no one watching
content: The essay does not say self-correction is only private, and this book is the argument that it is not: the sequences on expressing your concerns, on lonely dissent, on evaporative cooling and on Asch are about the social machinery of error-catching. What the astronaut image says is that the precaution must not be performed for an audience, which is the distinction between a discipline and a display, and it is the same distinction the intellectual-humility scale draws. Mercier and Sperber's theory also does not say that solitary reasoners cannot double-check an instrument; it says they are bad at criticizing their own conclusions, which is a different operation from adding a redundant cable.

quote: because physicists have this arrogant idea that their models should work all the time, not just most of the time, they follow up on small flaws
content: The history is the essay's case rather than against it. Le Verrier quantified Mercury's anomaly and hunted Vulcan for it precisely because the discrepancy was intolerable to a physicist who expected the model to work to arcseconds; the solar-neutrino deficit was chased for thirty years by people building larger and larger detectors rather than declaring three-eighths close enough. That is following up a small flaw, at enormous cost, for decades, with the wrong hypothesis in hand — which is what the essay is describing and what Lakatos is describing. A discipline that tolerates an anomaly while continuing to measure it is not the same as one that never noticed.

quote: The problem is motivated skepticism a.k.a. disconfirmation bias
content: The Tappin–Druckman confound is real and it is a confound, not a refutation: it establishes that asymmetric scrutiny is consistent with unmotivated updating, not that motivation is absent. The evidence that separates them exists and goes the essay's way. A meta-analysis of ninety-one selective-exposure studies found a reliable preference for congenial information that grew with commitment to the belief and with the defensibility of the position, which is a pattern about motivation, not about priors (Hart et al. 2009); and myside bias in argument evaluation is uncorrelated with cognitive ability, which a purely prior-driven account does not predict (Stanovich & West 2008).
